cards.text: Job has lost his children, his wealth and his health. For chapter after chapter he's argued with his friends and asked for a hearing with God, and then a young man named Elihu jumped in with a long speech about storms and thunder. Now, finally, after ALL that talking, the LORD Himself answers Job.

cards.question: When the LORD finally answers Job, where does His voice come from?

answers.text: Out of a pillar of cloud

cards.question: The LORD's very first question to Job praises him for speaking with great knowledge.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, “Now brace yourself like a man”. Job has wanted his day in court for chapters, friend, and court is now in SESSION.

cards.question: Now that the LORD is here, He tells Job that He will be the one answering Job's questions.

cards.text: First question: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?” That's like your new boss asking where you were when they poured the office foundation, and you started on TUESDAY.

cards.question: The LORD talks about the earth like a building. He asks who fixed its ___ and who laid its ___.
When the earth's cornerstone was laid, what were the morning stars and the sons of God doing?

cards.text: Next, the sea bursts forth from the womb, and the LORD makes the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket. God swaddled the OCEAN, friend, and I can't even wrap a cookie box with a whole mustache for hands.

cards.question: The sea comes bursting out with its proud waves. What does the LORD do with it?
The LORD speaks right to the sea and tells its proud waves where they must stop.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks if Job, in all his days, has ever commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place. Friend, most of us lose an argument with the snooze button every single morning.

cards.question: As the dawn spreads to the ends of the earth, the LORD says it shakes the ___ out of it.

cards.text: “The earth takes shape like clay under a seal” and its hills stand out like the folds of a garment. Clay under a seal, friend? That's STAMPING, that's my whole job, and God did it to a PLANET.
“Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.” Then the LORD's questions head down, WAY down, deeper than the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Heading down into the depths, where does the LORD ask if Job has journeyed?

answers.text: To the vents of the sea
To the bottom of the Jordan

cards.question: The LORD asks Job whether the gates of death have been revealed to him.

cards.text: The LORD asks if Job has surveyed the whole extent of the earth. Then He turns to light and darkness.

cards.question: The LORD talks about light and darkness as if each one has a ___ with paths leading to it.
The LORD tells Job, “Surely you know, for you were already born!” What is He pointing out?

answers.text: Job is older than the earth
Job learned it from his elders

cards.text: Now the LORD asks if Job has entered the storehouses of snow or seen the storehouses of hail. STOREHOUSES, friend, and I lose track of one little jar of sprinkles.

cards.question: The LORD says He holds the snow and hail in reserve for times of ___.

cards.text: Which way does the lightning scatter, or the east wind? Who cuts a channel for the flood and clears a path for the thunderbolt?

cards.question: The LORD says He sends the rain only to places where people live and can use it.

cards.text: Rain on a desert where no man lives, to “make it sprout with tender grass.” No crowd, no applause, nobody there to say thank you… and He waters it anyway.

cards.question: The LORD asks if the rain has a father and from whose womb the ice comes. What picture is He using for the weather?
The LORD says the surface of the deep never freezes.

cards.text: Now the LORD points up: can Job bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion? Friend, every cookie box I seal lights ONE star over my bakery, and I celebrate like I invented the sky.

cards.question: The LORD asks if Job can lead out the Bear and her cubs, or bring forth the ___ in their seasons.
Still looking at the sky, what does the LORD ask if Job knows?

answers.text: The names of all the angels

cards.text: Then the LORD asks if Job can command the clouds so that a flood of water covers him.

cards.question: The LORD asks Job whether the lightning bolts report to him, saying “Here we are”.

cards.text: Picture lightning bolts clocking in for their shift, calling out “Here we are”. Friend, I can't even get my oven timer to report to me.

cards.question: In the middle of all the sky and weather questions, what else does the LORD ask about?

answers.text: Who put wisdom in the heart

cards.text: Then He asks who has the wisdom to count the clouds. I counted the dust falling in that junk drawer for YEARS, friend, and I never once got a final number.

cards.question: The LORD asks who can tilt something in the heavens to pour down rain. What does He picture up there?
The heavens' water jars get tilted when the ___ hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Job is still standing in that whirlwind, and this conversation is far from over.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 5 quotes "make it sprout with tender grass.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states several facts from outside the passage with no reference: Job losing his children, wealth and health (Job 1-2), the long arguments with his friends and his request for a hearing with God, and Elihu's speech (Job 32-37). The card cites only Job 38:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card calls Elihu's speech "a long speech about storms and thunder." Elihu speaks for six chapters (Job 32-37), mostly about God's justice and Job's words. Storms come up only near the end (Job 36:27-37:24), so this description stretches the text. It also hints at the whirlwind answer on card 2.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "Job has wanted his day in court for chapters" states a fact from outside the passage (for example Job 13:3, 23:3-7, 31:35) with no reference. The card cites only Job 38:3.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Blank 1 ("who fixed its ___") asks the baker to guess the wording "measurements." Nothing earlier lets them reason it out over "roof," which also fits "fixed." This tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "And God did it to a PLANET" turns the comparison in Job 38:14 ("The earth takes shape like clay under a seal") into a statement that God stamped the earth. The verse is a simile about how the earth takes shape at dawn. It does not say God pressed a seal on it.
This story card only retells Job 38:35 ("Here we are"), which card 12 already covered. It adds no new part of the passage and does not move the baker forward.
